items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: listening to all of that is what got me to where I am today and I believe it was probably L’il Jazz (Roy Eldridge), and Charlie Shavers, you know, just the sound of the trumpet you know.

ctx.x: Can I ask you why you wanted it? What was it that might have been going on in your household or in your neighborhood or on the radio perhaps that made you want to get your hands on that cornet?

Well by the time I was five years old my mom had a genuine Victrola, you know, just like the ones that are in the museum. And she had the Jazz at the Philharmonic recordings by Norman Granz. You know? Pretty hip for that time. And I’d sit myself down and put that big arm on those thick 78s and listening to all of that is what got me to where I am today and I believe it was probably L’il Jazz (Roy Eldridge), and Charlie Shavers, you know, just the sound of the trumpet you know. And of course Dizzy Gillespie. And I…
in and get it. And above it was some sheet music of Dizzy Gillespie you know, and I’m saying oh boy, this is right up my alley.
